subsystems.drivetrain: SDS MK4i, tuned in stages before adding odometry and vision correction.
subsystems.intake: Protected under-bumper pickup selected for collision resistance.
subsystems.transfer: Polycord conveyance feeds the central pivot assembly.
subsystems.scoring: Pivoting mechanism covers acquisition, speaker and amp; independently driven shooter sides add note spin.

versions: Climb was unreliable at Gwinnett; spool/assist and intake work between Week 3 and Albany improved climbing/trapping.
dossier.analysis: Highly relevant PCH precedent: protect the main scorer, then use the gap between events to improve a secondary capability. Their fabrication choice supports rapid repair and iteration.
limits: Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.

context_documents.title: 2024-1771 · Low moving mass and rapid prototyping support a multi-task pivot
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1771: Low moving mass and rapid prototyping support a multi-task pivot

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A protected under-bumper collector and polycord conveyor feed a central pivoted scoring assembly. Motors sit near the pivot and long belt runs carry power outward. Independent shooting sides provide note spin; the same mechanism serves ground pickup, speaker and amp poses.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source describes selecting objectives at kickoff, prototyping multiple launcher types and using short print/test iterations to resolve problems. Its under-bumper choice emphasizes collision protection.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Moving motors toward the pivot can reduce rotational inertia, but long belts introduce compliance, tension and replacement considerations. A shared pivot simplifies the number of mechanisms while making each pose and connecting motion more important. Rapid printed iterations are a development capability that another team must budget for, rather than assume it receives by copying the final CAD.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure belt-related angular lag and shot variation after fast pivot moves. Reproduce the complete pickup-to-score path, and include repair/reprint time in the architecture comparison.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/GWJxVlSt0uE](https://youtu.be/GWJxVlSt0uE)

source_reviews.title: North Gwinnett team website
facts: The team calls its 2024 robot Toothless.
source_reviews.limitations: Gallery caption does not identify component construction.

source_reviews.title: 2024 symposium program
source_reviews.review_basis: Read symposium session text attributed to Team 1771
facts: The session describes availability, easy tooling, fast iteration and impact/vibration absorption as reasons to consider wood in FRC.
source_reviews.limitations: General claims are not material specifications or proof that any named Toothless part used wood.

source_reviews.title: North Gwinnett Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Older dossier only. Full captions were unavailable.
facts: The dossier describes a routed wood structure, under-bumper intake, polycord conveyance, pivoting scorer and modified telescopic boat-hook climber.
source_reviews.limitations: Team interview mechanism details and event chronology were not re-read directly.

source_reviews.title: FIRST season record
facts: Autonomous Award at Gwinnett, Albany, district championship and Daly.
source_reviews.limitations: Awards do not validate a routine or count individual actions.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Toothless is an inherited example of routing a floor note through a protected low entry to a scorer that changes angle for different destinations. The symposium text supplies the team's general material reasoning independently of the older interview synopsis. The design question is whether a wood assembly holds the pickup, transfer and shooter in alignment through repeated replacement, humidity and contact. Easy fabrication only helps if the repaired assembly preserves those relationships.
piece_flow: The inherited description puts the pickup beneath the bumper and uses polycord to advance the note.
The central pivot assembly receives the note at a feed pose and repositions it for speaker or amp.
The inherited sequence pairs the modified telescoping hook with trap access after climbing.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: A low entrance protects the collector from some direct contact but brings it near the carpet and bumper supports. The feed position needs a repeatable stop or calibration because conveyor-to-pivot misalignment can change retention and release. Add climb loads to the packaging drawing because high hook forces can enter the same chassis that sets shooter alignment.

subsystems.name: Structure, pickup and feed
subsystems.construction: Older dossier describes routed wood, a protected pickup and polycord transfer.
subsystems.operation: Capture from the floor and retain the note through the handoff.
subsystems.team_rationale: Protected pickup was attributed to collision resistance. The symposium independently explains the team's broad case for wood.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Define the load-carrying joints and replacement datums. Local bearing crush or moisture movement could matter before a member visibly breaks.
subsystems.interfaces: Floor height, bumper opening, transfer belt line and pivot home position.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Proposed checks include replacement time, alignment after replacement and reversal with a folded note.
subsystems.unknowns: Wood grade, joining details and exact capture dimensions.

subsystems.name: Scorer and climber
subsystems.construction: Inherited pivoted scorer with independent wheel drive and telescopic hook with modified spool and constant-force assist.
subsystems.operation: Position and launch the note. Reach, engage and pull against the chain for the endgame pose.
subsystems.team_rationale: Older dossier attributes spool and assist work to climbing problems at Gwinnett.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An assist may help the hook reach, while reliable loaded retraction also depends on spool winding, end stops and chassis pose. Validate deployment and lifting separately.
subsystems.interfaces: The extended hook and trap release pose must clear the scorer and stage.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect line stacking, guide friction and rapid access to the spool after a failed extension.
subsystems.unknowns: Spool dimensions, line anchorage and event-level success rate.

revisions: Inherited account places a climb and pickup revision between Gwinnett and Albany. Official awards provide event context only.
transferable_principles: Use low-cost replaceable plates where joints retain alignment. Audit one repair before assuming the material makes the whole robot easier to maintain.
Evaluate autonomous route selection by verified branches and acquisition outcome. A combinatorial count does not quantify robust coverage.
disconfirming_conditions: Wood may be a poor fit where joint bearing stiffness, water exposure or loaded dimensional repeatability dominates.
A compact protected opening loses value if it misses notes during ordinary defended approaches.
remaining_gaps: Full interview, as-built structure and climber drawings, exact change dates and autonomous logs.

Loaded climber/spool detail and feed pose of pivot assembly
